Implement procedural WebGL2 bird/pipes/ground/sky, resize/DPR and context loss/destroy lifecycle. Use browser_test to verify rendering. Read the applicable specs and current source before editing. After changes, inspect relevant interactions and use the supplied run_tests. Additional self-written tests are optional and limited to at most three small cases per pure module. Use the real browser tool instead of DOM/WebGL mocks. Use efficient edits for small corrections. Browser stages must also use browser_test. Do not change protected specs or acceptance harness. All prior functionality must remain working. Coordinate reference for this stage: logical pixel coordinates have a top-left origin. Convert every vertex exactly once to clip coordinates: clipX = 2*x/logicalWidth - 1; clipY = 1 - 2*y/logicalHeight. Pass the actual state.config.width and height when using helpers, or perform this conversion explicitly in the vertex shader. Vertex counts are counts of vertices: two floats per XY position means length/2; use the complete stride for interleaved attributes. The ready scene also draws the bird and enough details for at least four distinguishable colors. If a real browser color check fails, inspect finite vertex values, conversion, attribute stride and draw count. Fix your geometry rather than modifying browser prototypes, getContext or readPixels. Keep real WebGL drawing and all lifecycle requirements.

If a check fails, inspect only the relevant source snippets using read_file line ranges and fix that issue. Avoid whole-file audits, duplicate regression tests and replacing whole files for small corrections. Stop with a brief final status when the game is complete. No editor, replay or extra features. Keep all earlier contracts working; specifications and the external harness are protected.
